notes:
TRADING CHECK FIRST: theinside.com is fully live and trading as of 2026-08-19 - homepage returns HTTP 200 with a live Stripe key (pk_live_...), live PayPal client id, an active site-wide 25% sale banner, and a footer copyright of 2026. It remains a Havenly-owned brand (footer lists Havenly, Interior Define, The Citizenry, St. Frank, Burrow). No wind-down. robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Disallow:' (fully permissive, no Claude-specific rule).

ACCESS: The site is a Laravel + React SPA behind Cloudflare; raw curl of any page returns only the app shell, and WebFetch/Googlebot-UA also get only the shell (no prerender service is triggered). r.jina.ai was NOT usable this session - it returned a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' interstitial (HTTP 403) on every attempt across three retries, so the route that carried the prior Home-Decor pass was unavailable. Two routes were used instead: (1) I pulled /js/app.js plus all 171 lazy chunks from /js/chunks/, which contain the hard-coded mega-menu arrays and a canonical category-URL map, and (2) the site's own unauthenticated GraphQL endpoint https://www.theinside.com/graphql (Apollo uri:'/graphql' found in app.js), which serves the exact payloads the listing pages render: categoryProductsBySlug(slug) for /c/<seo>/<slug> pages and merchandiserBySlug(slug) for /collections/<handle> pages. Every count was then re-verified by rendering the real page in Chrome and counting distinct /products/ tiles.

CATEGORY TREE SOURCE: the live mega-menu, extracted verbatim from app.js (arrays 'no' = Furniture menu with columns Bedroom / Living Room / Dining Room / Quick Ship, and 'oo' = Outdoor menu with a column titled 'Furniture'), cross-checked against the Shop-All category tile map in chunk 160.js (v/x objects) which adds an Office column containing Desk Chairs. Nav labels rendered in the browser confirm the top-level bar: New, Furniture, Decor, Window, Bedding, Outdoor, Fabric, Inspiration, Free Swatches, Trade.

QTY METHOD: the site publishes NO product count anywhere - no 'N products/items/results' string exists on any listing page (regex-checked on every page rendered in Chrome, all returned zero matches), no pagination and no Load-More control. So qty is §4 method 3, full enumeration. The listing pages are not paginated: they render one tile per subcategory that has stock (a bed model is one tile with a size selector, not four size rows) plus every product in the page's featuredProducts block, which renders inline in the same grid (verified NOT a carousel - zero product links sit inside a .slick-slider on any page). I therefore computed tiles = (subcategories with >=1 product) + featuredProducts from the GraphQL payload and then verified the number against a live Chrome render for all 18 leaves; every single one matched exactly. Independent corroboration: the same GraphQL method returns 33 for /collections/lighting, identical to the 33 the prior Home-Decor pass established by three separate rendered fetches.

WHAT I REJECTED AND WHY:
- Algolia (app U5ARNXNU5F, index production_products, key in page source) reports 75,241 hits and category facets like Beds=63,625. That index is fabric x size variant-level and bears no relation to what any page displays - not used for any qty.
- Mattresses & Foundations (/c/bedroom-furniture/mattresses-and-foundations, 2 tiles: The Euro Top Mattress, The Foundation) excluded per the brief - mattresses and bed foundations are bedding, and Beds is a separate node so no forced take applies.
- 'End of Bed Benches' in the Bedroom column points at the very same URL as Living Room > Benches (/c/living-room-furniture/benches); recorded once only, under Living Room, to avoid the duplicate-link defect. /c/bedroom-furniture/benches is a third SEO alias for the identical page (the route's first path segment is cosmetic and ignored by the router).
- §3 roll-ups dropped: /collections/furniture (Shop All Furniture, 17), /collections/new-furniture (46), /collections/new-arrivals, /collections/bestsellers, /collections/outdoorliving, /collections/the-bedroom-edit, /collections/decor.
- Non-furniture nav nodes dropped: Throw Pillows, Curtains, Bedding, Wallpaper, Table Linens, Throw Blankets, Rugs, Lighting, Fabric by the Yard, Outdoor Pillows, Outdoor Rugs, Pickleball Paddles (a product page).
- Categories that exist in the schema but are dead or unreachable, so not emitted: Room Dividers (/c/home-decor/room-dividers, 0 products), Cabana Stools and Cabana Bundles (/c/outdoor-furniture/..., 0 products each), Accent Tables and Nightstands as /c/ categories (0 products - the nav routes these to /collections/ pages instead), Bed Foundations (0), Mattresses (0). Bedroom Sets is a live category holding 6 furniture sets, but it has NO site-published category URL - it is absent from the mega-menu, from the Shop-All map and from every chunk, and sitemap-bedroom-sets.xml lists only the 6 product URLs - so rather than invent a /c/<segment>/bedroom-sets URL I left it out; flagged here for manual review.
- Quick Ship is a genuine nav column, not a filter view: its five category pages carry a completely different frame assortment from the made-to-order pages (e.g. Quick Ship Beds = Tailored Platform / Art Deco / Square Back / Classic Wingback / Regency, none of which appear on the Beds page), so they are recorded as real leaves with no double counting of frames.

OVERLAP TO BE AWARE OF: /collections/coffee-tables-and-side-tables (38) is composed of 22 Accent Tables + 2 Coffee Tables + the same 14 Nightstands that the Nightstands leaf counts. Both are separate nav leaves so both are recorded; the 14 nightstands are counted twice across those two rows because the site itself lists them on both pages. A parallel merchandiser page /collections/accent-tables (35 = 21 accent tables + 14 nightstands) exists and is used by the Shop-All page, but the primary mega-menu points at coffee-tables-and-side-tables, so that is the URL recorded.

SANITY CHECKS RUN: (a) counts differ per category, never constant; (b) the h1 of every page loaded was read and matches the category requested (no silent parent fallback); (c) no round/capped numbers; (d) no page has pagination or a Load More, and scrolling to the bottom added nothing; (e) the featured blocks were confirmed to be in-category products rendered in the main grid, not a cross-sell carousel; (f) every leaf was counted twice - once via GraphQL, once via a live DOM render - and all 18 agreed.
